title: Implement the credential split with its migration
description:
Implement exactly what the design tick decided. If you find yourself redesigning, stop and say so on the tick rather than quietly choosing differently — the design was written down so this tick would not have to guess.

THE CARE THIS NEEDS, beyond the mechanics: the file holds live GitHub OAuth refresh tokens and a Cloudflare API token on real machines. Anything you write must be safe to run twice, safe to run on a file that has already been migrated, and safe to run on a file that has never seen a factory. Never write a partially-migrated file — write the new shape completely or leave the old one untouched.

File permissions matter here and are easy to lose in a rewrite: ~/.ticksrc is 0600 and must stay 0600 after any write. Check what the current code does before changing how the file is written.

Also handle the duplicate parser per the design: internal/tickboard/cloud/client.go reads ~/.ticksrc with its own hand-rolled readConfigFile() and never imports internal/ticksrc. Whatever the design chose, do not leave two parsers of one format with no contract.

DO NOT touch cmd/tk/cmd/upgrade.go — a sibling tick owns it.
acceptance_criteria: The split is implemented as designed. ~/.ticksrc keeps 0600 after any write. Migration is idempotent — running twice, or on an already-migrated file, or on a file with no factory keys, all behave correctly and are tested. No partially-written file is possible. The duplicate-parser decision is implemented. go test ./... green.
closed_reason: Completed: internal/ticksrc is gone, and no ticks package outside internal/factory names a KeyFactory* constant — both verified by direct check, not by reading the diff. The factory owns ~/.ticfacrc with its own duplicated credential code, and the merge-and-drain migration runs at every factory entry point.
